definitions.explanation: A sum of money imposed as punishment for breaking a law, rule, or regulation. Used in both legal and informal contexts.

examples.japanese: {駐車違反|ちゅうしゃいはん}で{罰金|ばっきん}を{取|と}られた。
examples.english: I was fined for a parking violation.

examples.japanese: {飲酒運転|いんしゅうんてん}には{高額|こうがく}の{罰金|ばっきん}が{科|か}せられる{可能性|かのうせい}がある。
examples.english: Drunk driving can result in a heavy fine.

notes: Common collocations: {罰金|ばっきん}を{払|はら}う (to pay a fine), {罰金|ばっきん}を{科|か}す / {罰金|ばっきん}が{科|か}せられる (to impose a fine / to have a fine imposed), {罰金|ばっきん}{刑|けい} (fine as a criminal penalty). In Japanese law, {罰金|ばっきん} is a formal criminal penalty, distinct from {反則金|はんそくきん} (infraction penalty — the administrative fine for minor traffic violations). Informally, {罰金|ばっきん} is used casually for any monetary penalty, even playful ones among friends. Related: {科料|かりょう} (minor fine — a lighter criminal penalty), {違約金|いやくきん} (penalty for breach of contract).
